sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 19.02.2021.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 19.02.2021 at about 3.40 p.m., while he was riding the Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-03-HC-8868, on Hosur main road, near Konappana Agrahara junction, Electronic City, Bangalore i.e., from Electronic City and proceeding towards Hosa road, the driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No. RJ-18-GB-5929 by driving it in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the petitioner's scooter, caused the accident and as a result, petitioner fell down on the road and the left front wheel of the said lorry ran over on his right leg.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Cauvery hospital for first aid and thereafter he was shifted to Hosmat hospital, Bangalore wherein he took treatment as inpatient and in spite of best treatment given by doctors petitioner's right leg amputated above thigh level.

It is stated that he has spent Rs.6,00,000/- for his treatment, medicine etc.,
3.

It is further stated that prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as Civil Engineer (Supervisor/consultant) at M/s M.R. Consultant and earning Rs.45,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not able to do his work as doing earlier and lost his income.
It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No. RJ-18-GB-5929.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the insurer and 2nd respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 entered appearance through its learned counsel and filed its written statement.
The respondent No.2 has not appeared before the tribunal, hence he has been placed exparte.
5. The 1st respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
Also denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner.
It has also denied the amount spent towards medical expenses by the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and contended that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner.
It has contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid driving license and hence it is not liable to pay compensation.

The respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.RJ-18-GB-5929 and contended that its liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it has contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, on all these grounds sought for dismissal of the petition.

7. Based on the pleadings, following issues are framed:-

No. KA-03- HC-8868, on Hosur main road, near Konappana Agrahara junction, Electronic City, Bangalore, within the limits of Electronic City Traffic Police Station, the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No. RJ-18-GB-5929 and dashed to the scooter of the petitioner, resulting into motor accident due to which petitioner sustained injuries in the accident.

FIS, Sketch, Spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, 133 notice, reply and charge sheet at Ex.P1 to 9 and in the cross of PW-1 he has admitted that at the time of accident he was proceeding from Electronic city to Hosa road and the offending lorry was going towards Bangalore bearing No.RJ-18- J V-5929 which came and dashed from backside.

Petitioner further has examined Mrs. Shanthamma Medical Record Officer of Hosmat hospital as PW.4 and got marked inpatient record as per Ex.P33 to 38.

The said witness has been cross examined by the respondent No.2 counsel in which she has admitted that the injured came to their hospital immediately after the accident and they have given intimation to the police.

15. Whereas, the respondent No.1 has filed written statement and contended that the accident has taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner himself and hence they are not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner, but have not led any defence evidence.

16. On perusal of the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex. P9 are the certified copies of FIR, Complaint, spot panchanama, sketch, IMV report, notice u/s. 133 of IMV Act, reply, Charge sheet and in the police records it is mentioned that on the relevant date, time and place stating that petitioner on 19.02.2021 at about 3.40 p.m., while he was riding the Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.
KA-03-HC-8868 at that time the driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No.RJ-18-GB-5929 came in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the motor cycle of the petitioner, caused the accident and as a result,
petitioner sustained injuries.
Further the above documents also clearly discloses that the charge sheet is filed against offending lorry.

17. In view of my discussion, I am of the opinion that it can be safely held that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving on the part of driver of lorry bearing Reg.No.RJ-18-GB-5929, due to which petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the road accident.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE No:-2: In this issue burden is on the petitioner to prove that, he is entitle for compensation as prayed.

While answering issue No.1, I have held that on the relevant date, time and place, the accident had occurred due to negligent act of the offending vehicle and as a result the petitioner has sustained injuries.
Now it is to be seen that whether the petitioner is entitle for compensation?
If so for how much and from whom.
Whereas injuries causes deprivation to the body which results in losses entitling claimant to claim damages.
Further damages may vary according to the gravity of the injuries and the said damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. Pecuniary and Non-pecuniary damages.
Pecuniary damages are those like medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning and future loss of earning.
Non-pecuniary damages includes for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering, loss of amenities in life.

Therefore, considering the overall documentary evidence I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income and also has proved he was getting salary of Rs.42,000/- per month at the time of accident-.

Hence, looking into the nature of injuries as well as the age of the petitioner as 24 years showing his occupation as Civil Engineer the income of the petitioner is considered as 42,000/- it will meet the ends of justice.
DISABILITY:

The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and produced the medical documents at Ex.P6 and 10 & 11 and he has also contended that he had sustained injuries of "right lower limb above knee amputation done for the injury of extensive degloving injury,
right thigh all compartments and right femur type 3 C fracture, right proximal tibia fibula fracture. " which is grievous in nature and and the said injuries are also depicts in the medical documents produced by the petitioner.
Further petitioner has contended that due to the said accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled person.

In support of his contention petitioner had examined the doctor as PW.2 Dr. S.
Ramachandra and being non-treated doctor has deposed that petitioner has sustained grievous injurious and due to the said injuries petitioner has become permanently disabled person and he has assessed permanent physical disability to right lower limb to an extent of 85%.

Further the disability assessed by the said doctor is with respect to the particular limb and injuries caused to the petitioner as per Ex.P10 discharge summary and the hospital bills are showing that the petitioner has sustained " right lower limb above knee amputation done for the injury of extensive degloving injury, right thigh all compartments and right femur type 3 C fracture, right proximal tibia fibula fracture." which are grievous in nature.

Whereas PW.2 in his cross has admitted that, he by using artificial limb it will be helpful for the petitioner through out his life for his day to day work and also with the assistance of artificial limb he can sit and do the computer work.

Further he admits that the stump portion in the thigh is about 23 c.m. and has only assessed physical disability and not effect on his avocation due to disability and further as the petitioner is a Civil Engineer it will effect 100% on his job.
Under these circumstances the disability assessed by PW.2 will have to be carefully scrutinized.

In this regard, I would like to rely upon decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in Rajkumar Vs Ajaykumar & another in 2011 ACJ 1, wherein it is clearly laid down that at the time of assessing the physical disability the loss of future earning capacity on account of such disability is something which has to be necessarily proved by the injured by himself with other cogent evidence which would,
in turn dependent upon other facts such as nature of injuries sustained, nature of treatment, quantum of disability and more importantly the nature of avocation of the Mr. Akshay S vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195334952/

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court had further held that the doctor has necessarily stated about the nature of disablement, whether it is of permanent nature, or a temporary disablement or a partial permanent disablement and the extent of mobility and stability component.

However, PW.2 has assessed functional permanent physical disability with respect to right lower limb to an extent of 85%, above knee amputation of the right lowe limb at 85% by observing that petitioner complains of pain of unable to carry out his profession as Civil Engineer, unable to walk normally, unable to sit down, sit cross legged and squat.

Whereas if disability leads to any restriction or lack of ability to perform an activity in the manner considered normal for human being and the said permanent disability refers to the residuary in capacity or loss of use of some part of body, found existing at the end of period of treatment.

After achieving the maximum bodily improvement or recovery which is likely to remain for the remainder life of the injured, then such injuries sustained in motor accident can be considered as permanent disability for the purpose of claiming compensation.

However, it is also settled principle of law that different parts of body have different percentage of disability and loss of future income would depend upon the fact and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.

Thus, considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the disability assessed by PW.2 who is non-treated Doctor and also he has admitted in his cross-examination that he has only assessed disability and not given treatment to the petitioner, the total extent of disability to the whole body and looking at the disability assessed by non-treated doctor towards the right lower limb to an extent of 85%,
above knee amputation of the right lower limb at 85% and the said disability is permanent in nature and the said pain of the disability will be throughout the life of the injured person which will effect his health and avocation.

As such considering the above aspects of crush injury resulting in above knee amputation of right leg and disability to right lower limb and the avocation of the petitioner shown as Civil Engineer and by considering the age of the petitioner as 24 years and looking into the disability assessed by the non-treated doctor @85%.

Further as per the schedule - I of workman compensation act resulting into permanent partial disablement of loss of amputation below hip with stump exceeding 12.70 cms in length measured from tip of great trenchanter is considered at 80% and as such in this case also even though PW.2 is a non- treated doctor, but considering the disability of amputation of right above knee along with his avocation as Civil Engineer the permanent disability of 80% it will meet the ends of justice.

sentences.text: 22. CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT, ATTENDANT CHARGES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES.:-
Petitioner has stated that he has taken treatment in the hospital as inpatient and to prove the same he has produced Ex.P10 & 11 discharge summaries of Hosmat hospital

reveals that petitioner has sustained right lower limb above knee amputation done for the injury of extensive degloving injury, right thigh all compartments and right femur type 3 C fracture, right proximal tibia fibula fracture.
The doctor has opined that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

That the petitioner has taken treatment in the said hospital from 19.02.2021 to 26.02.2021 and from 11.09.2021 to 12.09.2021 and underwent right above knee amputation stump exicision of ulcer and bony overgrowth with flap cover.
As per those documents the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for about 10 days.

Considering those documents produced by the petitioner in all he has taken treatment for about 10 days as inpatient and in the said period of treatment necessarily one person should have attended them in the hospital.

Thus looking at the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the document produced by him and with regard the age of the petitioner an amount of Rs.1,000/- per day can be considered as appropriate amount towards the head of attendant charges, food and conveyance during their stay in the hospital.
Hence totally PW.1 is entitled for 10,000/- (1,000 X 10) towards attendant charges, food and conveyance.

23. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE PERIOD OF TREATMENT:-
On perusal of the medical documents it goes to show that petitioner has sustained amputation injuries and he had taken treatment for about 1 0 days as inpatient in the hospital and the petitioner would have lost his income for a period of at least 3 month.

Such being the fact, the loss of income during the said period has also to be compensated to the petitioner and while discussing above, monthly income of 42,000/- per month is considered and for 3 months under this head petitioner is entitled for 1,26,000/- towards loss of income during the period of treatment.
24. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner has deposed that he is aged 23 years and also as per Adhaar card his age is 24 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.

The petitioner has examined the doctor as PW.2 and he has assessed disability of left lower limb at 85%
and also this court has considered the said disability @80% to the whole body.
PW.2 has stated that due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner has difficulty in doing routine activity.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.1,00,000/- on this head.

In this case respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
